content:
Ava: Heads-up — I'm consolidating the Optimize toolkit quant + caching examples into a single 'patterns' section so users don't hop between pages. Draft PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4387

Marcus: Nice. Can you include a short explainer for when to prefer kv-prefetch vs. prefix caching? Those decisions are tripping up a few customers in support.

Ava: Yep. Thinking a tiny decision table and two micro-examples (one low-latency short-seq, one high-throughput long-batch). Will also add a one-liner about quantization tradeoffs.

Jin: Small ask — the JS SDK snippet in the current docs uses the old `optkit.applyQuantProfile('short_seq')` call. We've standardized on the options object shape. Example should be:

```js
const opt = new OptimizeOptions().withQuantProfile(QuantProfiles.short_sequence())
client.configure(opt)
```

Jin: Also can we add a tiny Rust snippet? Some infra teams use it for internal tooling. One line to show the builder chain is enough.

Ava: Good call. I'll add both JS and Rust. Rust example will be very short, like:

```rust
let opts = OptimizeOptions::builder().quant_profile(QuantProfile::short_sequence()).build();
client.apply(opts);
```

Marcus: For the kv-prefetch anchor there was a stale `#prefetch` anchor referenced from the long-batch guide — link-bot flagged it. Can you update to `#kv-prefetch-policy` and add an inline note about default TTLs?

link-bot: Link validation: found 1 broken anchor -> docs/optimize/kv-prefetch.md#prefetch. Suggested replacement: #kv-prefetch-policy.

Ava: I'll fix the anchor and add TTL note (default 10m in hosted, configurable in Dedicated). Also adding a migration note: users referencing the old optkit field `QuantProfile.ShortSeq` should switch to `QuantProfiles.short_sequence()` across SDKs.

Jin: One more nit — in examples we sometimes show `batch_size: auto`. Can we instead recommend `batch_size: \"auto\"` (string) in YAML snippets to avoid parsing surprises in some renderers?

Ava: Good catch. Will normalize the YAML examples to quote auto.

Marcus: If you want someone to proof the wording after you push, ping me. I'll do a quick pass on the decision table and the TTL blurb.

Ava: Thanks — pushing in ~30m. Marking this thread as in-progress. I'll post the PR link when ready and request reviews from @Marcus and @Jin. :rocket:
